answer: The protocol requires agents to maintain 1,000 unique data shards for identity, verified by unpredictable retrieval audits. An honest agent incurs a baseline storage cost, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 times that expense to mirror distinct content. Like a clear crystal defining structure, the verifier requests random shards at every epoch. Similar to the cooling of basalt, these shards are hardened as fixed records. Any failure to return segments during the tide of incoming requests triggers an immediate, non-refundable slash, ensuring the cost of faking identities remains strictly.
